Premier Ben Carroll says $230m would be earmarked for 10 public dental clinics to operate on a walk-in basis Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Victorians would be able to walk into a dental clinic and receive free checkups and treatment under an Australian-first proposal the Labor government will take to the November state election. The premier, Ben Carroll, will announce the plan – Labor’s first major election commitment – at a rally on Saturday to mark fewer than 100 days until Victorians go to the polls. Carroll will say a re-elected Labor government would spend $230m to open 10 public dental clinics across the state, where oral care clinicians would be able to provide free checkups and treatments, including fillings, root canals and extractions.

“Labor can’t staff the dental services we already have, yet want Victorians to believe they can suddenly provide free dental care for seven million people,” they said. Asked about high vacancy rates among dentists on Saturday, Stitt told reporters the government would have more to about “the workforce component of this election commitment”. The Victorian Greens said the announcement of a “handful of free dental clinics shows that Labor only acts on the cost of living when it faces electoral wipeout”. “It’s a start – but with only enough places for a stadium’s worth of Victorians, getting an appointment will be harder than scoring Taylor Swift tickets,” said health spokesperson, Dr Sarah Mansfield. The Victorian Council of Social Service (Vcoss) welcomed the announcement, but called on the government to ensure “that these ser ---

Carroll described the plan as “structural cost-of-living support” and a national-first intervention by a state government. “Only Labor will deliver free dental care for all Victorians,” he said in a statement. On Saturday, Caroll told reporters the government was aiming to have the 10 clinics open by the middle of 2027. The health minister, Ingrid Stitt, has described the plan as the dental equivalent of the state’s urgent care clinics, where people can “turn up and get the care you need”. “Getting dental care shouldn’t be determined by your bank balance or where you live,” Stitt said. Following the announcement, an opposition spokesperson said the government’s “mismanagement of our health system” meant the median waiting time for public dental care in Victoria was seven months, compared to one month in NSW, according to Productivity Commission data.

Premier Ben Carroll says $230m would be earmarked for 10 public dental clinics to operate on a walk-in basis

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victorians would be able to walk into a dental clinic and receive free checkups and treatment under an Australian-first proposal the Labor government will take to the November state election.

The premier, Ben Carroll, will announce the plan – Labor’s first major election commitment – at a rally on Saturday to mark fewer than 100 days until Victorians go to the polls.

Carroll will say a re-elected Labor government would spend $230m to open 10 public dental clinics across the state, where oral care clinicians would be able to provide free checkups and treatments, including fillings, root canals and extractions.

Carroll described the plan as “structural cost-of-living support” and a national-first intervention by a state government.

“Only Labor will deliver free dental care for all Victorians,” he said in a statement.

On Saturday, Caroll told reporters the government was aiming to have the 10 clinics open by the middle of 2027.

The health minister, Ingrid Stitt, has described the plan as the dental equivalent of the state’s urgent care clinics, where people can “turn up and get the care you need”.

“Getting dental care shouldn’t be determined by your bank balance or where you live,” Stitt said.

Following the announcement, an opposition spokesperson said the government’s “mismanagement of our health system” meant the median waiting time for public dental care in Victoria was seven months, compared to one month in NSW, according to Productivity Commission data.

“Labor can’t staff the dental services we already have, yet want Victorians to believe they can suddenly provide free dental care for seven million people,” they said.

The Victorian Greens said the announcement of a “handful of free dental clinics shows that Labor only acts on the cost of living when it faces electoral wipeout”.

Victorian Premier Ben Carroll is promising a $230 million free dental care package if Labor is re-elected as part of a strategic shift that aims to put health, education and crime at the centre of the party’s campaign.

The cost-of-living relief is likely to alarm global ratings agencies that have cautioned both sides of politics against big spending sprees in the lead-up to the November 28 election, as the state budget groans under net debt forecast to top $199 billion within four years.
